title: Investigating the Shortcomings of LLMs in Step-by-Step Legal Reasoning

task.approximation: prompt layout reconstructed from Figure 2 (section labels and format lines); the repository script adds a 'Task:' line with a system sentence that the paper does not print (open_points)

items.source: https://github.com/VenkyMishra/Legal-Reasoning (redirect of VenkyMishra/legal_reasoning); the Civ. Pro. data itself must be requested through https://github.com/trusthlt/legal-argument-reasoning-task (copyrighted Glannon Guide material)
items.license: unknown (dataset released on request under the trusthlt terms)

prompt.source_location: Figure 2 (answer-format template: Legal Context / Question / Options / format lines); example in Figure 18
prompt.verbatim: partial (the section labels and the three format lines are printed in Figure 2; their order and spacing are reconstructed and agree with the repository's zero-shot script)

output.parse: regex \[Final Answer[^\]]*\]\s*:?\s*([A-D]) on the last matching line, else the last standalone letter A-D

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of the 175 scenarios whose final option equals the correct option

open_points: no hook: the Civ. Pro. items (175 Glannon Guide scenarios) are released only on request via trusthlt/legal-argument-reasoning-task, i.e. gated; once obtained, place the file locally and a loader (items.inline or a hook) can be added in minutes - prompt, parse and accuracy are otherwise machine-ready.

the repository's inference script prefixes 'Task:' and 'You are a helpful legal assistant. Choose the correct option by performing legal reasoning while strictly adhering to the legal context below.' which the paper does not print; the paper-only version is the default here.
notes: Soundness and correctness columns of Table 4 need the GPT-4o auto-evaluator and are not targeted. ~1K input and ~500 output tokens per call.
